taxonomic_note: Kew POWO and Flora of North America accept Cynanchum unifarium. UT Austin Williamson County study and older references use Cynanchum racemosum var. unifarium. Do not collapse the whole C. racemosum species into this taxon; the varietal name is synonymous with this accepted C. unifarium concept.
look_here_first: Find the FLOWER CLUSTER where it meets an opposite-leaf node. Talayote has MANY very small (~5 mm wide) pale yellow-green flowers with WHITISH petal margins on a branching/racemelike AXILLARY cyme; larger Matelea milkvines have much showier netted or longitudinally striped flowers. An older plump smooth green follicle (7.5–9.5 cm long) and a line of short hairs running along each internode give excellent confirmation.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Current Kew POWO/FNA accepted distribution includes native Texas, and UT Austin Vascular Plants of Williamson County supplies detailed local occurrence. A third independent target-county native voucher count has not been reviewed. Uvalde field photographs exist but not counted as voucher proof here.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Do not infer Hays/Travis target counties from State of Texas occurrence or user's unpublished observation totals. Range status separate from learner admission.

best_field_traits: Perennial vigorous herbaceous twining vine with white milky latex; many stems may arise from base
Stems usually cylindrical, tough, slender ~2 mm diameter, short-hairy, hairs often arranged as a LINE along each internode
Leaves opposite/decussate with petioles ~10–55 mm; blades deeply heart-shaped at base, often ~2–10 cm long with acute to acuminate tips
Axillary many-flowered racemelike cyme, often 10 or more tiny flowers, with secondary 1–2-flowered cymules and zigzag rachis
Flowers about 5 mm across, green-yellow with thin white margin around short petals, not the showy dark reticulate large green Matelea stars
Corolla campanulate-rotate, lobes ~3 mm, bearing inner marginal ridges; corona of five fleshy segments, 3-lobed near apex
Fruit large PLUMP smooth glabrous green follicle, not muricate, ~75–95 mm x 30–33 mm; commonly blunt toward tip
Seeds flattened with brown winged margins and a tuft of white silky coma hairs
morphology_keys.phenology: Regional flowering typically late spring into fall; field photo date and local weather should be considered.
morphology_keys.leaf_venation: Principal veins conspicuous and raised below; heart-shaped leaf form overlaps Matelea, Gonolobus and certain other Apocynaceae.
morphology_keys.latex_caution: White latex also occurs in Matelea and other milkvines; it is not a safe stand-alone genus discriminator.
field_identification_sequence: Photograph opposite nodes with both petioles and axillary flower cluster attached.
Include one close flower with a scale reference; distinguish tiny green-white lobes from big patterned Matelea flower faces.
Trace one branch of racemelike cyme; look for numerous small flowers and zigzag short branchlets.
Look for short hairs in a single line along green/red stem internodes using hand lens.
If fruiting, check pod for smooth inflated surface versus prickly/studded Matelea or angular Gonolobus.

comparisons.key_distinctions: M. reticulata bears much larger flat pale green DARK-NETTED corollas with a silvery central 'pearl' and roughened/muricate follicles. M. edwardsensis has larger pale green bell-like longitudinally striped flowers with dense hairs on their inner surface and a muricate pod. Gonolobus suberosus var. granulatus has relatively large non-reticulate uniformly olive-green flowers and SMOOTH but sharply angular fruit; talayote flowers are much smaller and its follicle plump/smooth without the strong angles. Cynanchum laeve has CLEAR latex vs talayote WHITE latex in Flora of North America; consult flowers/corona as well. Funastrum flowers/corona structure differ; do not decide from twining leaves alone.
